name: Where large banks stand
description: Independently sourced lines on how named banks describe third-party AI agent access to a customer's login. Reported marks a press report. The file does not copy the BankingNewsAI institution table.
attribution: The Agent Economy bank account access (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/bank-account-access.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.
title: Where large banks stand
framing: Large banks have been blocking or restricting third-party AI agents from using a customer's banking login to transact. Some describe a limited read-only path through approved open banking providers. Agent-owned accounts and single-use cards are compared in the table on this page.

tracker.title: BankingNewsAI, any third-party agent
tracker.note: The page fetched on 2026-11-16 says it is updated weekly, that the last sweep was November 15, 2026, and that the institution record was checked 2026-11-10.

examples.stance_summary: A spokeswoman told CNBC on October 13, 2026 that the bank blocks external AI agents from operating on behalf of retail customers.
examples.sanctioned_path: Agents may have limited read-only access, for example balances, through customer-authorized open banking connectors such as Plaid. They cannot send money or pay a bill.
examples.source_title: CNBC, JPMorgan AI agents account access, October 13, 2026

examples.stance_summary: A Citi spokesperson wrote to USA TODAY on October 23, 2026: We do not permit third-party AI agents or assistants to log into a customer's account or transact directly within our digital banking platforms.
examples.sanctioned_path: The same statement says customers may authorize limited, read-only access through certain Citi-approved open banking providers.

examples.stance_summary: The bank's update page says the Online Access Agreement change is effective November 24, 2026, and that the bank reserves the right to restrict or block access from certain third-party AI tools. Section 15 treats instructions from an AI agent you authorize as yours. You remain responsible until you notify the bank of revocation under Section 17(d).
examples.sanctioned_path: Section 15 applies when you authorize an AI agent to access the service or an eligible account. The pages checked do not describe a separate read-only open banking connector.

examples.stance_summary: PCWorld on November 13, 2026 quotes an email from Ashley Ross telling customers not to share a username or password with an AI-enabled tool or agent. The article says the bank has stopped short of banning third-party agents from logging into customer accounts.
examples.sanctioned_path: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The PCWorld article does not describe a read-only open banking path for Bank of America.

examples.stance_summary: The Paypers on November 10, 2026 reports that HSBC, Nationwide, NatWest, Barclays, and Lloyds have moved to block AI agents from accessing customer accounts.
examples.sanctioned_path: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. The Paypers article does not describe a read-only open banking path for those banks.

examples.stance_summary: USA TODAY, citing a Bloomberg interview on October 16, 2026, reports that CEO Rick Wurster said the firm is blocking between tens and twenties of attempts by major AI agents to access and manipulate client funds.
examples.sanctioned_path: Not documented as of 2026-11-16. That USA TODAY passage does not describe a sanctioned open banking path for Charles Schwab.
